findings.description: mark_invalid writes to the file for impression.served_at.date(), and for_day builds the invalid set only from that same day's file. This works only if the caller passes the original Impression. The marker also depends on served_at being in the same timezone as the day used in append. That is fragile but consistent, so the main risk is that an invalid record has no 'campaign' key and any other reader of the log that indexes record['campaign'] will raise a KeyError.
findings.suggestion: Include the campaign id in the invalid record, and make every reader skip records with kind == 'invalid'.
findings.title: Invalid marker is written to the day file derived from the impression's served_at, but for_day reads only the requested day's file

findings.description: can_bid calls spend(), which calls log.for_day(). That opens and JSON-parses the entire day file, and the file grows with each impression. eligible() does this once per campaign for every bid request, so the hot path is O(campaigns * impressions_today) disk I/O per request. The previous in-memory counter was O(1).
findings.suggestion: Cache per-day spend in memory, loading it from the log once and updating it on record/refund, or keep a per-campaign index.
findings.title: Every can_bid call re-reads and parses the whole day's log file
